content: It achieves this by relaxing the blood vessels, allowing blood to flow more easily throughout the body. In some cases, it may be prescribed for other conditions, so it is important to consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. Hydralazine is available in tablet form and is taken orally. It is typically administered two to four times daily at evenly spaced intervals. You should follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully and ask your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. It is crucial to take hydralazine exactly as prescribed, without altering the dose or frequency. You should continue taking the medication even if you feel well, and you should not stop taking it without consulting your doctor. If you are considering using this medication for these purposes, discuss the potential risks with your doctor. Before starting hydralazine, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to hydralazine, aspirin, tartrazine (a yellow dye found in some foods and medications), or any other drugs. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are taking, including indomethacin, metoprolol, propranolol, and any vitamins. Let your doctor know if you have a history of coronary artery disease, rheumatic heart disease, kidney or liver disease, or if you have ever had a heart attack. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. If you become pregnant while taking hydralazine, contact your doctor immediately. Additionally, if you are scheduled for surgery, including dental procedures, inform your surgeon or dentist that you are taking hydralazine. Ask your doctor about the safe use of alcohol while on this medication, as alcohol can exacerbate hydralazine’s side effects. Hydralazine should be taken with meals or a snack. Your doctor may recommend a low-salt or low-sodium diet, and it is important to follow these dietary instructions carefully. If you miss a dose of hydralazine, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Hydralazine may cause side effects. Minor side effects include flushing (a sensation of warmth), headache, upset stomach, vomiting, loss of appetite, diarrhea, constipation, eye tearing, nasal congestion, and rash. If these symptoms are severe or persistent, inform your doctor. Serious side effects require immediate medical attention. These include fainting, joint or muscle pain, unexplained fever, rapid heartbeat, chest pain, swelling of the ankles or feet, and numbness or tingling in the hands or feet. If you experience any severe side effects, you or your doctor can report them to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program. Store hydralazine in its original container, tightly sealed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture, and do not store it in the bathroom. Dispose of any expired or unused medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for guidance on disposal. In the event of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. If so, request instructions from your doctor or pharmacist. Do not share this medication with anyone else, and consult your pharmacist if you have questions about refilling your prescription. Hydralazine is also available in combination products, such as Hydra-Zide®, which contains hydralazine hydrochloride and hydrochlorothiazide.
